statement: 1. One AI model can run in several places, called deployments, that share one public name.
story_cause: A company can run one AI model in several places, called deployments, that share one public model name
note: RSELECT-001: get_model_list concatenates all deployments under one model_name.

statement: 2. The router's job is to choose which place serves each request.
story_cause: For each request, this part of the router finds every deployment that could serve that name
note: Purpose section of the spec: decides which concrete deployment of a model group serves a request.

statement: 3. First it lists every place that could serve the requested name.
story_cause: For each request, this part of the router finds every deployment that could serve that name
note: RSELECT-020 name resolution precedes the filters (RSELECT-040 step 1).

statement: 4. Then filters remove places that are unhealthy, resting after errors, paused, or kept for another team.
story_cause: Filters can then drop deployments that are unhealthy, resting after recent errors, paused, or reserved for another team
note: RSELECT-043 (health, only when health-check routing is on, RSELECT-142), RSELECT-044 (cooldown), RSELECT-046 (paused), RSELECT-024 (reserved for another team).

statement: 5. From what is left it picks one at random, unless another strategy is set.
story_cause: By default the router picks one of the rest at random
note: RSELECT-067/RSELECT-139: simple-shuffle is the default, weighted random by weight/rpm/tpm when set, else uniform; other strategies ask their selector (RSELECT-068).

statement: 6. If nothing is left, the caller gets a 429 error, meaning no deployment could take the request.
story_cause: When the filters leave none, the caller usually gets an error with status 429, which here means no deployment could take the request
note: RSELECT-054/RSELECT-283: RouterRateLimitError, status 429. Not universal (400 for an unknown name, other errors when pre-call checks or plugins empty the list), but the story said 'usually' and the statement is true for the main case.

statement: 7. There is a full path and a shorter path that skips some checks, such as the team filter.
story_cause: Selection has a full path and a reduced path that skips several checks
note: RSELECT-128: sync selection does not run the team and web-search filters, hook, callback checks, tag routing, plugin narrowing.

statement: 8. Only the router-wide strategy setting picks the path; five named strategies, including the default, get the full path.
story_cause: router-wide strategy | the strategy setting of the whole router; it alone decides between the full and reduced paths
note: RSELECT-060: only the router-level routing_strategy is checked, five names listed, simple-shuffle default (RSELECT-139). Overstated on its own because sync calls take the reduced path whatever the strategy (RSELECT-121) and async pass-through always runs the hook (RSELECT-130); statement 9 covers sync, so the pair is true.

statement: 9. Image generation through the synchronous method always gets the short path.
story_cause: Synchronous selection, such as sync image generation, always takes the reduced path
note: RCALL-106 (sync image_generation uses the sync selector) and RSELECT-121/RSELECT-128.

statement: 10. Some model names are really redirectors that send a request on to another model before the lookup.
story_cause: On the full path, the router first lets that strategy router move the request to one of its tiers, another model name
note: RSELECT-015, RSELECT-061, RSELECT-092: the hook runs before the healthy-deployment pipeline and its model replaces the requested one. Only on the full path.

statement: 11. After errors, a deployment rests for a while, five seconds by default.
story_cause: cooldown | a pause after recent errors during which selection skips a deployment, 5 seconds unless the router sets another length

statement: 12. Some settings can be changed while the router runs, but many are silently ignored.
story_cause: Other settings keep the values the router was built with, and the update leaves only a debug log line
note: RSELECT-152/RSELECT-252: only the runtime-updatable keys apply; others are dropped with a debug log 'Setting <name> is not allowed'.

statement: 13. Danger: with provider-budget-routing, every request for a model fails.
story_cause: One wrong setting can fail every request for a model.
note: RSELECT-279: for a model outside any routing group every request that resolves to a candidate list raises the no-deployment error; only a request by deployment id works. The statement drops the 'outside any routing group' qualifier, which the story's Watch-out keeps, but it is not a decision-changing omission.

statement: 14. Danger: with usage-based-routing, customers quietly lose team and rate-limit checks.
story_cause: Under one such as usage-based-routing, asynchronous calls skip the strategy routers, team filter, affinity and rate-limit checks, whatever strategy its routing group names
note: RSELECT-278 (impact: affinity, prompt-cache, rate-limit, auto-router logic and the team filter silently do not run) and RSELECT-128.

statement: 15. The wait time in the 429 error is the cooldown length, not the time actually left, so it can mislead.
story_cause: The wait in the no-deployment error is the configured cooldown length, not the time left
note: RSELECT-283: smallest configured cooldown length of the group's deployments, not the time remaining.

statement: 16. I assume the end caller notices a 429; the chapter does not say who reads the info log.
story_cause: On the full path, the router also writes this failure to its info log
note: The claims say the router logs at info and raises the 429 to its caller (RSELECT-054), and that configured fallbacks can still serve the request afterwards (RDISP-124, RDISP-101), so whether an end caller ever sees the 429 depends on fallbacks; the claims never say who reads the info log. Neither half is contradicted.

statement: C1. When you run the same model in several places under one name, our router works out which places can take each request, drops the ones that are unhealthy, paused, resting after errors or reserved for another team, and picks one at random.
story_cause: Filters can then drop deployments that are unhealthy, resting after recent errors, paused, or reserved for another team
note: True of the filters and the default pick (RSELECT-043/044/046/024, RSELECT-067). The customer line drops the story's 'can' and 'by default': dropping unhealthy places needs health-check routing on (RSELECT-142), and the pick is random only under the default strategy. Not contradicted.

statement: C2. If every place is out, your caller gets a 429 error, which here means nothing was available.
story_cause: When the filters leave none, the caller usually gets an error with status 429, which here means no deployment could take the request

statement: C3. Before I promise team limits or rate limits, I would check your strategy setting with engineering, because some settings skip those checks and one of them fails every request.
story_cause: reduced path | selection without the pre-routing hook, team and web-search filters, callback checks or tag routing
note: The advice is sound (RSELECT-278: the strategy name usage-based-routing skips the team filter and rate-limit checks; RSELECT-279: provider-budget-routing fails every request for a model outside a routing group). But 'team limits' names nothing in the claims: what is skipped is the team filter, which decides which team's deployments a caller may use, not a team limit or budget. A customer-facing promise built on 'team limits' is too loose to act on.

lost: model group versus routing group versus deployment
fix: Define the three once in the plain layer with one example: the model name 'gpt-4o' is the model group; dep-0 and dep-1 behind it are deployments; a routing group is a named bundle of several model names that share one strategy. Use 'model name' in plain text and keep 'model group' to the glossary.

lost: team and caller
fix: Before the first 'reserved for another team', say in one sentence that the caller is whoever's API key sent the request and a team is the group that key belongs to; deployments can be owned by a team.

lost: access group and the caller's key
fix: Say in plain words that an access group is a label on deployments and a key can be limited to certain labels; the lookup then keeps only deployments carrying an allowed label.

lost: pre-routing hook ... hook or a tier
fix: Write 'the first step on the full path' instead of 'hook' in plain text, and say 'a tier is one of the other model names the strategy router can send the request to'.

lost: strategy router ... auto, complexity, adaptive and quality routers
fix: Give one concrete sentence: a name such as 'smart-router' is not a model; it looks at the request and sends it on to another model name. List the four kinds only in the reference part, or say they are four ways of choosing.

lost: tier params
fix: Either drop the term from the glossary, or add its body sentence to the glossary row: the chosen tier can set values such as an output-token limit on the request, overwriting the caller's own.

lost: session binding
fix: Mark it in the first words as 'only for Claude Code traffic; ignore it otherwise' and move it out of the main glossary.

lost: common resolution
fix: Use 'name lookup' in the body and the glossary, and keep `_common_checks_available_deployment` as the code name only.

lost: lar1 ... usage-based-routing-v2 versus usage-based-routing
fix: State that the chapter does not say what lar1 and usage-based-routing do; only that these three accepted names make async calls take the reduced path while usage-based-routing-v2 keeps the full path, and add no recommendation beyond 'check which name the router is using'.

lost: callback checks ... stream continuation
fix: Say 'callback checks are extra filters registered by the proxy or the operator that run before the pick'. Gloss stream continuation as 'resuming a half-finished streamed answer on a deployment that can continue it' (RSELECT-123), or drop it from the example list.

lost: affinity
fix: Add the one-line reason from the AFFINITY claims for when it matters, for example a follow-up call that must return to the deployment that served the earlier one.

lost: pass-through flag and pass-through endpoints
fix: Define pass-through endpoints in a clause at first use (the proxy routes that pass a request to a provider's own API) and say a deployment must be marked for them (RSELECT-130 to RSELECT-135).

lost: selection trace ... Is a trace a monitoring tool? Who looks at it?
fix: Say in plain words that it is a timing record in the operator's tracing tool, of interest only to someone debugging; move it to Watch out.

lost: logging object
fix: Replace with 'the request's own failure logging', and say it receives the error on the full path only.

lost: structured-output setting
fix: Say what it tells a customer: a request that asks for structured (JSON-shaped) output can be refused with a 400 when every deployment of the group would reject it and drop-params is off (RSELECT-205, RSELECT-208).

lost: Redis ... shared Redis server
fix: On first mention say Redis is the shared cache server some routers attach to, run by whoever operates the router, and that other applications may use it too.

lost: wildcard route ... from its start
fix: Replace 'from its start' with the example: the pattern openai/*-mini matches openai/gpt-4o-mini and also openai/gpt-4o-mini-extra, because only the start of the name has to match (TARGETS-007).

lost: generic fallback list ... literal star key
fix: Say 'a catch-all fallback list, written under the single character * in the fallbacks setting, meaning for any model'. The router uses its first name for a name that matches nothing.

lost: order ... as an order fallback does
fix: Give an example: dep-0 has order 1 and dep-1 has order 2; selection uses only dep-0 while it survives; dep-1 serves only when the request names order 2, which an order fallback does after dep-0 fails.

lost: exclusion lists ... failover or a retry
fix: Say that when a call fails and the router tries again or moves to another deployment, it hands selection the ids it already tried so they are skipped.

lost: provisioned-throughput share
fix: Use an example: a deployment with reserved capacity is split among teams; a team that holds a share can use only the deployments it has a share in; a team with none can use only deployments that have no shares.

lost: access window ... who sets it
fix: Say it is set in the deployment's configuration by whoever configures the router and give the example from the error text: 'reserved for another team until 17:00 Europe/Berlin'.

lost: reset call
fix: Introduce 'reset' as the router method that clears its state before the cache-flush row mentions it, or drop the mention.

lost: allowed-failures policy and health-check routing ... how a customer sets them
fix: Say both are router settings set at build time by the operator, not per request and not changeable by the settings update, and name the failure-handling chapter for what they do.

lost: a synchronous call always takes the reduced path (figure sends it to 'Routing plugins configured?')
fix: Add to that sentence: 'and the reduced path refuses a router that has routing plugins', so the text and the figure agree.

lost: every reduced-path call fails before any lookup
fix: State the consequence outright: on a router with routing plugins, synchronous calls such as sync image generation fail, and so do asynchronous calls on a strategy name outside the five (RSELECT-120).

lost: Asynchronous pass-through selection skips this check and always runs the pre-routing hook
fix: Move to its own sentence labelled 'pass-through endpoints use a separate selection call that always runs the first step, whatever the strategy' (RSELECT-130), and say the figure is about ordinary calls.

lost: Only the router-wide strategy counts here ... Strategy seems to mean two different things
fix: Say once that the same setting name does two jobs: the router-wide value decides the path, while a routing group's or a request's value only decides how the final pick is made.

lost: Ordinary deployments keep unmatched traffic: Suppose no router matched so far, tag filtering is on, every strategy router under the name has tags, and the name also has ordinary deployments
fix: Lead with the rule, then list the three conditions as bullets, then add one example with names: requests whose tags match nothing normally go to the first strategy router; they go to ordinary deployments only when tag filtering is on, every strategy router has tags and ordinary deployments exist.

lost: replaces the requested model and messages ... the caller's own messages stay unchanged
fix: Say: for the rest of selection the router uses the tier's model and the tier's version of the messages; those messages are not written back, so your original messages are untouched (RSELECT-076).

lost: an error about paused dep-0 names openai/gpt-4o
fix: Say who sees it (the caller, in the error text) and that the error shows the provider model, not the id the caller sent.

lost: That error names no provider, so the configured fallbacks can still serve the request
fix: Say the fallback step stops at errors tied to a specific provider (and a few other cases, RDISP-101); this 400 names none, so the fallback step carries on.

lost: looks for deployments whose provider model string equals the name
fix: Add: some callers send the provider's own model string, such as openai/gpt-4o, instead of the public name; the lookup tries that as a last resort.

lost: This seems to contradict 'Resting deployments drop out'
fix: State the default first: resting deployments are removed and an empty list gives the 429. Only when health-check routing and an allowed-failures policy are both set does the router keep the resting ones (RSELECT-045). Say the worked example uses default settings.

lost: A model group with one deployment still goes through every filter, so its paused deployment ends in the 429 instead
fix: Add a two-row table: asked by deployment id and paused gives the 503; asked by model name with its only deployment paused gives the 429. Say callers using model names (the normal case) get the 429.

lost: the text "true" does not count
fix: Say plainly that a config writing "true" in quotes does not pause the deployment and that the chapter documents no warning for it.

lost: the caller usually gets an error with status 429
fix: Replace 'usually' with the cases: 429 when filters empty the list; 400 when the name matches nothing; other errors when pre-call checks or routing plugins empty the list.

lost: starts a 60-second cooldown ... nothing says why
fix: Add a timeline row for the failed request that starts each cooldown, and say the example router has a cooldown length of 60 seconds.

lost: 5 seconds unless the router sets another length ... the example uses 60
fix: Say in the example's title or first row that the router's cooldown time is set to 60 seconds, and name that setting.

lost: build-time cooldown default ... as when all are paused
fix: Replace 'build-time' with 'the cooldown length the router started with; changing cooldown time later does not change it', and say a group whose deployments are all paused has no cooldown entries.

lost: a fallback to another model whose own plugin pass narrows nothing can fail
fix: Add a concrete case: request for A, plugin narrows to A's models, A fails, fallback to B, B's plugin pass narrows nothing so A's list still applies and B ends with no deployments left (RSELECT-276).

lost: The reduced path calls no failure handlers ... what gets logged where
fix: Replace the paragraph with a small table: path by info log, failure handlers, selection trace, error line in the retry loop, and say these are for an operator reading logs.

lost: stores 0, which calls then skip as unset
fix: Say 'a timeout of 0 means this setting puts no time limit on the call' (RCALL-083), so the lost half-second limit is obvious.

lost: how a customer finds out which strategy they are on
fix: Add: read the router-wide strategy from the router's settings; get_settings returns its live value (RSELECT-150).

lost: which looks like a defect ... Is it fixed?
fix: Rephrase: 'the spec flags this as unintended; the code at the audited commit fails every such request', and add 'avoid this strategy name for models outside routing groups'.

lost: info log ... warning
fix: Say these lines go to the router's server log, read by whoever operates the router; the spec names no other reader.

lost: Which of these settings does a customer control
fix: Add a line or column: router settings are set by whoever operates the router; per request, callers can only pass tags, a specific-deployment request, and a strategy override.

lost: silently ignores keys ... only a debug log line ... No rollback
fix: Say there is no error or warning to the administrator, only a debug line, and that get_settings shows what took effect; and that a bad value stops the update after earlier keys were applied.

lost: Why does 'Asking for a deployment by its id' skip cooldowns?
fix: Say who sends requests by id (callers that must reach exactly one deployment) and that the skip is how the code behaves, with no claim that it is a customer feature.

lost: Who can trigger it? Is it part of the 'reset call'?
fix: Say flush_cache is a router method called by code that holds the router, that reset also runs it (RSELECT-184), and that the spec does not say customers can call it.

lost: Words you'll see ... about 45 entries
fix: Split the glossary into a short list of terms the plain layer uses and a reference list for the rest; delete terms that appear only in the glossary.

lost: Claim IDs run through nearly every sentence
fix: Put claim ids at the end of each paragraph or in the reference layer, not mid-sentence in the plain text.

lost: which here means no deployment could take the request is repeated
fix: Say it once at first use and write just '429' afterwards.
